To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HIV-infected patients, naïve for antiretrovial therapy and with a low CD4 cell count, can develop neurocognitive disorders, and that the presence of these neurocognitive disorders is associated to higher levels of inflammatory cytokines in the central nervous system, but not with higher levels of HIV RNA.
intrathecal immune system activation, but not higher HIV-RNA, is present at baseline in advanced HIV-infected patients who are naïve to ART and who are diagnosed as having HAND.
HIV RNA in CSF and plasma was reduced by ART in HIV-infected patients but that intrathecal immune activity was not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HIV-RNA and intratechal immune system in HAND of HIV-infected naïve patients with advanced disease.
a possible role of intratechal cytokines and chemokines in the pathogenesis of HAND and their potential role in the pathogenesis.
the role of intrathecal immune response in HIV-1-associated neurological disorders in advanced HIV-1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HIV RNA is not a good predictor of HAND, whereas intrathecal immune response is a good predictor of HIV-associated neurocognitve disorders.

HIV-associated neurocognition disorders in advanced naïve patients are associated with intrathecal immune system activation, which does not seem to be related to HIV-RNA in the central nervous system.

Intrathecal immune activation and HIV-RNA levels in the cerebrospinal fluids of advanced naive HIV-infected patients: A role in the development of HIV-associated neurocognition disorders
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV-associated neurocognition is a multifactorial disorder, in which the intrathecal immune response, rather than the virus, plays a pivotal role.
HIV RNA is not associated with neurocognitive impairment and that immune activation is a major factor for the development of HIV-associated neurocognitve disorders.
the intrathecal inflammatory cytokines are a better marker for HAND in advanced HIV-infected patients, whereas CSF viremias are not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intrathecal immune system is not affected by ART in advanced naïve patients with HAND.
intrathecal immune-activation parameters are associated to HAND in naïve HIV-infedted patients with advanced disease.

HIV-infected patients, even in the absence of a history of ART and at the moment of diagnosis, may already have developed neurocognitive impairment, which is associated with intrathecal immune system activation, rather than with intrathecal HIV-RNA.
